0 Quartermaster General: East Front In June of 1941, Germany, along with Finland, Romania, and other Axis nations, invaded the Soviet Union. Germany sought another lightning victory, like those attained in Poland, France, and elsewhere. Four years and millions of lives later, Soviet troops captured Berlin and forced the German surrender. Quartermaster General: East Front portrays this struggle between the Soviet Union and Germany, with its associated forces — known herein as the “Pact”, after the Tripartite Pact. This two-player game is played over 16 seasonal game rounds, from Summer 1941 through Spring 1945. The game is won by accumulating Victory Points (VPs), most of which will be awarded for controlling geographical objectives during the four annual scoring rounds. If you’re ahead by 10 or more VPs at the end of a scoring round, you win immediately; otherwise, the game continues until the final scoring round, when the player with the most VPs wins. [Rating: 2/10] Disagree with others. I love the original. This game is too luck dependent. It is too easy to not get reinforcements as the russian player early on, or poor draws with the german.  With the original you are working with a hand of seven. Here a smaller hand. And if you get the wrong cards…sucks to be you. Little to no planning. Just reaction to the crap cards you draw.  A quicker game would be to just draw cards and play them in a ‘war’ like manner.  Terrain, like the marshes, mountains, etc. Has no effect in this game.

[Rating: 3/10] This is the only game in the series I've played and it was obnoxious. Deterministic combat feels terrible. A 5 card hand feels tiny in this game, especially when everything is onetime use. That means you're usually stifled in what your able to do. It was less making lemonade out of lemons and more throwing cards into the trash. At no point did I feel clever in my card play. I don't recommend this and I won't be checking out anything else QMG.  Looking for a lightweight wargame? Pick up Hammer of the Scots, 300 Earth and Water, Memoir 44 or Undaunted. You'll have more fun.

[Rating: 5/10] Initial Impressions: It does sort of have logistics of keeping a contiguous path back to your bases as pseudo-supply lines. There is certainly a lot of room to play better with the specific card effects here. But unfortunately, the game seems to be too much of a battle of attrition, even with the Nazis being a rush faction and the Soviets being a slow buildup. The combat especially of just removing pieces back and forth causes the game to have that feeling.

[Rating: 5/10] Played on BGA.  Well designed game that runs too long and may be too confrontational.

[Rating: 5.5/10] BGA. Game is interesting, but very imbalanced. Quite straightforward, low risk winning strategy for Russians while Germans need to play risky and aggressively from the very beginning. This also quickly makes the game quite repetitive, as there seem to be not many successful strategies.

[Rating: 6/10] My final opinion on this game is that I will play it "to pass time" on BGA but nothing more. There are just too many problematic choices within this design that I do not feel it can be recommended for competitive players. Imbalance in wargames is nothing new, but this is one of the most unbalanced games I have ever played (reminded me of the first print of Cry Havoc in a way), and not in a "fun" way.
